history.sg_progress: While the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs initiates the recruitment process approximately three months prior to the adoption of sanctions renewal resolutions, challenges in identifying qualified candidates – particularly in ensuring gender balance and geographical diversity – have been a key factor contributing to delays in submitting expert panel proposals to Security Council sanctions committees within the designated two-week time frame. To address this, the Department is intensifying its engagement with Member States to expand the pool of qualified candidates. In 2024 and 2025, targeted outreach efforts were made, including briefings to regional groups, virtual information sessions and direct bilateral consultations. These initiatives aimed to raise awareness of opportunities to serve on expert panels, clarify selection criteria and encourage the timely nominations of diverse and highly qualified individuals. In October 2024, the Department participated in an Impactpool virtual career fair for women in senior roles, alongside other United Nations Secretariat entities. This event, hosted by a career platform specializing in humanitarian and international roles, attracted 2,343 registered participants. Of those participants, 459 women from across all regional groups visited the joint United Nations Secretariat virtual booth, which featured presentations, fact sheets, videos and information on current openings for sanctions experts. The Department plans to participate in the October 2025 Impactpool session of the impact pool to continue promoting diversity in recruitment. In addition, in May and June 2024, the Department conducted briefings for representatives of the Group of African States, the Group of Arab States, the Group of Eastern European States and the Group of Latin American and Caribbean States. In May 2025, a similar briefing was held for the Group of Asia-Pacific States, with further briefings planned for the Group of African States and the Group of Arab States later in 2025. These efforts reflect the Department’s ongoing commitment to strengthening the recruitment process and ensuring inclusive representation across sanctions monitoring teams, groups and panels.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration intensify its efforts to ensure that expert panels are proposed to relevant sanctions committees in a timely manner.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Security Council Affairs Division of the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs has strengthened the recruitment of expert panels by starting the process three months before the adoption of sanctions renewal resolutions. It expanded outreach to Member States through briefings, virtual sessions and bilateral engagement (2024–2026), including dedicated events for Asian and Pacific and African States. A pool of experts was established (application link: https://careers.un.org/ jobSearchDescription/191928?languag e=en) as a candidate repository, supported by an annual note verbale to all Member States. The Security Council Affairs Division also engaged with the senior women’s talent pipeline and joined the 2025 Impact pool virtual career fair for senior women, attracting new candidates to the pool of experts. Despite these efforts, the recruitment of qualified experts within two weeks – while ensuring gender and geographical balance – remains difficult, as mandates and the required expertise continue to evolve.
history.board_assessment: Given the measures put in place by the Administration, the Board considers this recommendation implemented.
